chunks: And among what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿIsa, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthman, from Abi Jamilah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Salih, from Saʿd ibn Tarif, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام said: Whoever catches one rakʿah of the morning prayer before the rising of the sun has indeed caught the morning prayer in full.

Thus, the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as applying to one who has excuses and one who has a necessary need that prevents him from salat (prayer) at the beginning of the time, according to what we have already set forth regarding other prayers; this indicates that.

key_terms.أَوَّلِ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning of the prescribed prayer time
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer, meaning salat al-fajr
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, the endpoint mentioned for catching fajr

ai.seo_question: Does catching one rakʿah of fajr before sunrise count as having performed the prayer on time?
ai.summary: This report states that whoever reaches one rakʿah of salat al-fajr before sunrise is considered to have caught the prayer. The concluding statement explains that such reports are understood in the case of those with legitimate excuses or unavoidable necessity preventing prayer at the start of its time.
